incoming.explanation: The Mendon allotment is the second leg of the frontier-rights pattern.
The 1667 incorporation versus the 1662/3 death qualifies how John's name in the Mendon proprietors' record should be read - a right carried forward or retrospective, not proof of settlement.

finding.shortLabel: Ballou - John among Braintree men allotted at Mendon, 1662

sources.locator: History of the Town of Milford (1882), pp. 27-35

finding.statement: Adin Ballou's History of Milford places John Gurney among the Braintree men accepted to allotments at the new Mendon (Nipmug) plantation in 1662.

outgoing.explanation: The 1667 incorporation versus the 1662/3 death qualifies how John's name in the Mendon proprietors' record should be read - a right carried forward or retrospective, not proof of settlement.

finding.shortLabel: Open: Mendon post-1667 record vs John's 1662/3 death (right carried forward vs retrospective)

sources.locator: Proprietors' Records of Mendon (1899), pp. 13, 43, 46, 152-153 (John Gurny & Grisel Gurney as separate 20-acre lot-holders; post-1667 incorporation)

finding.statement: Because Mendon was incorporated only 15 May 1667 and John died 1662/3, his name in the printed Mendon proprietors' record stream postdates his death: it is most plausibly an early 1662 grant carried forward into the later proprietor list or a retrospective allottee entry rather than proof of residence. Whether the 1662 acceptance and the post-incorporation lot are the same right - and how 'John Gurny' and 'Grisel Gurney' as twenty-acre lot-holders relate to the widow/descendants - is developed in the family-Mendon-descendants topic; the manuscript proprietors' images remain the pull.
